section_summary: This section comprises U.S. Embassy Tokyo monthly political reports (Reports Nos. 124 through 128) and related State Department correspondence covering Japan from January through May 1937. It chronicles the collapse of the Hirota Cabinet, the installation and contentious tenure of General Senjuro Hayashi's administration, parliamentary conflicts, the unexpected dissolution of the Imperial Diet, and the ensuing general elections. Key international developments documented include U.S.-Japan negotiations resolving the long-standing perpetual leasehold system, cotton and hosiery export limitation agreements, Japanese economic goodwill missions abroad, Sino-Japanese tensions in North China, Soviet border and diplomatic frictions, and naval limitation policies. Domestic coverage highlights national budget expansion, gold shipments to the United States to support the yen, semi-wartime industrial controls, commodity price inflation, and spreading labor unrest.

subfiles.about: Concluding portion of the monthly report on political, economic, and military conditions in Japan during January 1937.
subfiles.summary: Contains the final sections of the Embassy's report for January 1937, analyzing the Army's dominance in Japanese politics, the resignation of War Minister Terauchi, and the Imperial selection of General Hayashi as Premier. Discusses domestic political realignment movements aimed at creating a new pro-military party, government finance challenges including deficit bonds and the introduction of foreign exchange control, and rising commodity prices. Concludes with a brief report on labor unrest at the Yawata Iron Works and comprehensive lists of despatches and telegrams sent to the Department during January.
subfiles.title: Report on Conditions in Japan during the Month of January, 1937 (Report No. 124)

subfiles.about: Monthly political report detailing internal Japanese politics, foreign relations, and economic conditions during February 1937.
subfiles.summary: Transmits Report No. 125 describing the formation of General Senjuro Hayashi's Cabinet, the replacement of stop-gap War Minister Nakamura by General Sugiyama, and the calming influence of Finance Minister Yuki. Examines foreign relations, including Premier Hayashi's conciliatory Diet address, reactions to the U.S. naval program, final ratification of the Osaka cotton textile agreement, President Quezon's visit, open-door policy discussions regarding the Congo Basin, and British perpetual leasehold negotiations. Reviews Diet debates featuring sharp interpellations by Yukio Ozaki and Seigo Nakano, the 1937-1938 national budget estimates, gold shipments, and notable labor disputes including the Tosa Steamship strike and the Meirokai union's nationalist agitation against NYK.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 2314: Report on Conditions in Japan during the Month of February, 1937 (Report No. 125)

subfiles.about: Monthly political report reviewing Japanese domestic politics, legislative actions, economic conditions, and foreign relations during March 1937.
subfiles.summary: Transmits Report No. 126 recording the formal diplomatic settlement of the perpetual leasehold question between Japan and the United States on March 25, 1937, alongside controversies over Japanese salmon fishing in the northeast Pacific. Analyzes Foreign Minister Naotake Sato's efforts to adopt a more conciliatory approach toward China and the USSR, which faced pushback from the military, and Japan's rejection of British proposals for 14-inch naval gun caliber limits. Chronicles the Diet proceedings where the record 1937-1938 budget was enacted, followed by Premier Hayashi's sudden dissolution of the Diet on March 31, as well as gold reserve shipments of ¥50,000,000 to New York and plans to place the shipbuilding industry on a semi-wartime footing.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 2368: Report on Conditions in Japan during the Month of March, 1937 (Report No. 126)

subfiles.about: Internal State Department memorandum highlighting significant points from the Tokyo Embassy's political report for April 1937.
subfiles.summary: Notes several key developments from the Tokyo Embassy's April report for State Department officials. Highlights the hosiery export agreement restricting Japanese shipments of socks and stockings to the United States to 1,500,000 dozen through 1939. Summarizes major diplomatic appointments including Suemasa Okamoto as Consul General at Shanghai, Eiji Amau as Minister to Switzerland, and Shigeru Kuriyama as Minister to Sweden, while observing widespread labor unrest caused by rising living costs.
subfiles.title: Division of Far Eastern Affairs Memorandum on Tokyo's Political Report for April

subfiles.about: Monthly political report surveying Japanese political affairs, Diet election results, financial measures, and diplomatic developments during April 1937.
subfiles.summary: Transmits Report No. 127 covering the April 30 Diet general elections, which resulted in losses for the traditional parties (Minseito and Seiyukai) and gains for the proletarian Shakai Taishuto, though leaving the non-party Hayashi Cabinet in power. Details relations with the United States, including the departure of the Kadono Economic Mission, friction over regulatory restrictions on American automobile assembly plants, and the hosiery export accord. Details international developments such as the settlement of the Keelung incident with Great Britain, trade friction with British India, perpetual leasehold agreements with France and Switzerland, the visit of a Chilean economic mission, and domestic economic measures including the duty-free import of steel, gold exports, and the establishment of the Cabinet Planning Board.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 2422: Report on Conditions in Japan during the Month of April, 1937 (Report No. 127)

subfiles.about: Diplomatic cover despatch transmitting the Tokyo Embassy's monthly report on conditions in Japan for May 1937.
subfiles.summary: Consists of Ambassador Joseph C. Grew's formal transmittal despatch No. 2462 to the Secretary of State, dated June 17, 1937, along with the title page of Enclosure No. 1, Report No. 128 (Report on Conditions in Japan during the Month of May, 1937). The full body of Report No. 128 continues beyond the end of this archival section.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 2462: Report on Conditions in Japan during the Month of May, 1937 (Report No. 128)
